advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether `request_stream` also needs a candidate span (or document that streaming is intentionally out of scope) so tracing coverage doesn't silently lapse if streaming is adopted.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/tracing.py:180: `async def request(` is the only Model method overridden in `_TracedCandidateModel`
ABSENCE: search for `request_stream` across src/rebar/llm returned no matches, and `run_stream`/`.run_stream` returned no matches, so no current caller streams — the gap is latent, not a live defect
WrapperModel delegates `request_stream` to the wrapped model, so streamed candidates would bypass the candidate span entirely
advisory.finding: The candidate-tracing wrapper overrides only `request`, not `request_stream`; if a streaming request path is ever used through the FallbackModel, candidate spans would silently not be emitted for streamed candidates.
scenarios: A future change routes structured or text ops through pydantic-ai's streaming API; failed streamed candidates become invisible again, silently regressing the observability this story adds.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that a `returned` candidate span carries `rebar.candidate.usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens` equal to the response usage.
evidence: `_ok_body` returns `"usage": {"input_tokens": 1, "output_tokens": 1}` (test_candidate_tracing.py:105) so these attrs ARE set on returned spans

ABSENCE: `search_files` for `usage.input`/`input_tokens` across tests/unit returns no assertion on the `rebar.candidate.usage.*` span keys — no test in test_candidate_tracing.py or test_candidate_tracing_oracle.py references these attribute names
A regression that stopped recording usage on the returned span, or recorded wrong values, would pass every test
advisory.finding: The candidate-span usage attributes `rebar.candidate.usage.input_tokens` and `rebar.candidate.usage.output_tokens`, emitted by `_CandidateHandle.returned()`, are never asserted by any test — an entire branch of the emitted span contract has zero regression coverage even though the happy-path `_ok_body` fixture returns a usage block that triggers their emission.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the happy-path or an oracle test, after collecting the `returned` span, assert `span.attrs['rebar.candidate.usage.input_tokens'] == 1` and the output-token equivalent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that `wrap_candidate(model, ...)` returns a wrapper whose `base_url`/`label`/`model_id` equal the wrapped model's.
evidence: tracing.py:166-178 comment: 'WrapperModel ... leaves these three base Model defaults in place, so forward them explicitly to stay fully transparent' with `base_url`/`label`/`model_id` property overrides

ABSENCE: `search_files` for `base_url`/`model_id` in tests/unit shows no test constructs a `_TracedCandidateModel`/`wrap_candidate` result and asserts these properties equal the wrapped model's values
The transparency contract these overrides exist to satisfy is asserted for none of the three properties
advisory.finding: The wrapper's `base_url`, `label`, and `model_id` delegating properties — explicitly documented as load-bearing to keep the wrapped model 'fully transparent' — have no test asserting they forward to `self.wrapped`, so a regression that dropped or broke these overrides would go undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Construct a fake wrapped model exposing distinct `base_url`/`label`/`model_id`, wrap it via `wrap_candidate`, and assert each property is delegated identically.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where `sanitize_diagnostic` yields no message and assert the raised span sets outcome=raised but omits `rebar.candidate.error`.
evidence: tracing.py:82-85 `except Exception: reason = None` then `if reason is not None: self._set('rebar.candidate.error', reason)`
test_candidate_tracing_oracle.py:200-217 (AC-7) exercises only the reason-present, sanitized path
ABSENCE: no test drives sanitize_diagnostic to fail/return no message and asserts the raised span still records outcome `raised` without an `rebar.candidate.error` attribute
advisory.finding: The `raised()` branch where the sanitized reason is `None` (sanitize_diagnostic fails or yields no `message`, so `rebar.candidate.error` is deliberately NOT set) is never exercised; only the reason-present path (AC-7) is tested, leaving the absence-of-error-attr contract unverified.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch `rebar.llm.failure.sanitize_diagnostic` to raise or return `{}`, run a failing candidate, and assert the span has `outcome == 'raised'` and no `ATTR_ERROR` key.
